members.title: Abstract — part 2
members.excerpt:
At the top-down interface, an empirically usable state or law is not a
context-free picture of everything. It is a receiver-faithful descent of a
stronger typed relational carrier through a declared experimental and
operational aperture. A successful theory is therefore like a lawful map: it
preserves specified observables and dynamics within a domain, forgets other
structure in explicit fibers, and has seams. A theory appears to fail outside
that domain when a previously merged fiber splits under a new probe, an
overlap adapter stops commuting, or the carrier's closure boundary is crossed.
The bottom-up relational construction, its O1 normal form, and this top-down
map contract are meant to meet at the same interface: the kernel is conjectured
to supply the common structure, the unique bare-dyad O1 `CAR` and retained
finite codebook supply exact coordinate charts, and the map contract explains
how correct domain theories can be partial without being mistaken. The charts
do not author topology, relation, operation, target law, or provenance.

That statement alone would be a useful language but not a new theory. The
nontrivial RPRM conjecture is that there is a **domain-independent, minimal,
composable repair rule** for such failures. Given an exact witness that a
receiver no longer preserves an admitted operation or observable, the rule
should classify the admissible minimal repairs and, where a unique or frozen
selector is promised, identify the selected new distinction, relation,
coordinate, generator, or receiver version needed to restore descent. If that rule can recover the
known reductions and interfaces of physics, constrain which extensions are
lawful, and make a prospective quantitative prediction, RPRM could mature
into a genuine unification theory. If it cannot, the universal claim fails.

The strongest current evidence is bottom-up. Alpha already has exact finite
forms of typed carriers, receiver-relative quotients, complete fibers,
transition descent, complementary lossy views, symmetry actions, mono

members.title: 7. Full closure and live seam
members.excerpt:
## 7. Full closure and live seam

```text
ROOT -> SELECT(supplied sigma) -> TYPE -> SOLVE/EXECUTE
     -> PROVE/TEST CAR-or-FOLD AND DESCENT -> REFINE or CLOSE/PROMOTE
     -> SEAL -> FLICK -> FOLD/INHERIT -> REOPEN.
```

The selection port remains explicit:

```text
sigma = (target, lens, branch, future, stopping rule, landing rule, authority).
```

A live seam remains `EVENT` until certified. Closure state and closure event are separate receivers. Publication is one atomic `FLICK` from a sealed prior root; failed landing leaves that prior root current, and `INHERIT` reopens only the affected dependency cone. Evidence closes by intersection, `V(E)=intersection_(e in E) S_e`; repetition is idempotent, and same-root views may refine a fiber without adding ancestry.

`EXACT`: typed finite completion; selected ordered-dyad `0|1` CAR; finite codebook addressing; finite deterministic receiver factorization/descent and the stated target/strong repair-alphabet minima; supplied finite-group residue; supplied radix trichotomy; supplied canonical finite path.  
`SCOPED`: affine, geometric, prime, pi, and domain adapters on named carriers.  
`OPEN`: global kernel minimality; target/law/topology authorship; one universal repair/composition rule; unbounded, continuous, stochastic, quantum, or physical closure.

**Strongest lawful totality:** RPRM is currently a finite typed calculus of construction, completion, lawful loss, future-preserving change, stated receiver-specific repair minima, atomic closure, and receipt-preserving reopen. Its universal generative and physical extensions remain open.
